prompt: Each seed of a certain tomato variety germinates with probability $0.6$, independently. A gardener plants $5$ seeds. What is the probability that exactly $3$ germinate? Round to four decimal places.
hint: This is binomial: $n = 5$, $p = 0.6$, and you want $P(X = 3)$.

hints.text: This is binomial: $n = 5$, $p = 0.6$, and you want $P(X = 3)$.

explanation: Binomial setting: 5 independent seeds, each germinates ($p = 0.6$) or not ($0.4$).

alternativeExplanations.title: One sequence, then count the arrangements
steps: One specific way: seeds 1, 2, 3 germinate and 4, 5 do not. Probability: $0.6 \cdot 0.6 \cdot 0.6 \cdot 0.4 \cdot 0.4 = 0.03456$.
But WHICH 3 germinate can happen in $\binom{5}{3} = 10$ ways, each with that same probability.
